sections.name: Header – Non-Surgical Spinal Decompression in Dow
sections.title: Non-Surgical Spinal Decompression in Downtown Austin

paras.t: For disc problems that haven't gotten better on their own. Casey Morgan D.C. looks at your imaging first, and only recommends decompression when it shows decompression fits.
Decompression is a slow, controlled stretch of the spine. It takes pressure off discs that have narrowed or bulged, and off the nerves they press on.
It's not an adjustment, and it's not surgery. It's a separate tool for a specific problem, which is why it starts with an evaluation, not a session.

callouts.title: Dr. Morgan does two things: adjustments and decompression.
callouts.text: No shockwave, no laser room, no four-machine circuit. When decompression is part of your plan, it works alongside your adjustments, not instead of them.

paras.t: Dr. Morgan recommends decompression when your X-rays show disc space narrowing or degeneration, or when pain is running down into a leg. That usually means one of these:

•  Herniated or bulging disc
•  Sciatica, or pain, numbness, or tingling down the leg
•  Low back pain that has lasted months and hasn't responded to other treatment
•  Neck pain from a disc problem

Who it's not for: Decompression isn't right for everyone. Dr. Morgan screens for things like severe osteoporosis, spinal fusion hardware, some advanced spinal conditions, and pregnancy. If it's not a fit, he'll tell you, and tell you what would help instead.

sections.title: How it works at West End

paras.t: No free first session, no hard sell after. We do a real evaluation first, and you decide with the price in front of you.

bullets.text: Your first visit: find out what's going on
bullets.body: Full history, a real exam, and any necessary digital X-rays, taken on site. Dr. Morgan shows you the imaging the same visit. If decompression might be part of the answer, he'll mention it then.

bullets.text: A few days later: the recommendation
bullets.body: Dr. Morgan walks you through what he found and what he recommends. If decompression fits, you get the number of sessions and the total price before you commit to anything.
Decompression sessions alongside your adjustments, on a schedule built around your week.

paras.t: If one of these sounds like you, decompression may be part of the answer.

cards.title: Herniated or Bulging Disc
cards.text: The structural problem underneath a lot of low back pain and sciatica.

cards.title: Sciatica
cards.text: Shooting pain, numbness, or tingling down the leg. Usually a disc pressing on a nerve.

cards.title: Lower Back Pain
cards.text: Pain that has lasted months and hasn't responded to other treatment.

cards.title: Neck Pain
cards.text: Neck pain, numbness, or tingling into the arm from a disc problem.

faqs.q: How do I know if I'm a candidate?
faqs.a: That's what the first visit is for. Dr. Morgan examines you, takes any necessary digital X-rays, and tells you whether decompression fits. If it doesn't, he'll say so.
No. Decompression is a cash service at $75 per session. Your first visit, with the exam and any necessary X-rays, can go through your insurance.

faqs.q: How many sessions will I need?
faqs.a: A typical plan is about 24 visits, but it depends on what your imaging shows. Dr. Morgan gives you the number and the total price after your evaluation, before you start.
Most people find it relaxing. It's a slow, controlled stretch, not a pop or a crack. If anything is uncomfortable, Dr. Morgan adjusts it.
Yes. Decompression works alongside your adjustments. Most decompression patients get both.

faqs.q: Is this an alternative to surgery?
faqs.a: Many people look at decompression before they consider surgery. It isn't a replacement for a surgeon's opinion, and if your imaging points to one, Dr. Morgan will tell you.

paras.t: Your first visit gets you a full exam, a consultation, and any necessary digital X-rays. You'll leave knowing what's going on, and whether decompression is part of the answer.
1611 W. 5th St., just off MoPac. Free covered garage parking. Monday through Thursday.
